//: The FOURTH typecheck program: the workbench stories.
Until 0.8.3 nothing typechecked a story at all, and it showed. The Button
story rendered `intent="danger"` — an intent `button.props.ts` explicitly
does not have — so `intentStyles['danger']` came back `undefined`, `cn()`
dropped it, and the workbench displayed an unstyled button labelled
"danger" as if that were the design. Nothing could catch it: stories sit
outside every other program, `storybook:build` transpiles without checking
types, and an unstyled button violates no axe rule. The workbench is the
instrument this repo trusts to show what a component looks like; an
instrument that silently renders a prop that does not exist is worse than
no instrument.
WHY THIS PROGRAM CAN HOLD BOTH LEAVES AT ONCE. A story imports each leaf by
its explicit path (`select.web.tsx` AND `select.native.tsx`), so unlike the
package's own programs there is no extensionless component specifier
needing two different answers. `moduleSuffixes` is still required for what
the leaves import of each OTHER: a `.native` leaf reaches
`../lib/native-theme`, which exists only as `native-theme.native.ts`. The
empty suffix comes FIRST so `./select.props` keeps resolving to
`select.props.ts` — the same ordering, for the same reason, as the
`resolve.extensions` list in `.storybook/main.ts`.
DOM lib and React Native types coexist here, exactly as they already do in
packages/design-system/tsconfig.native.test.json, and for the same reason:
`skipLibCheck` from the base. The web pane is React DOM, the native pane is
React Native primitives, and one story file contains both.
`react-native` maps to the REAL package's types rather than to
`workbench/react-native.ts`, which is what the runtime alias points at.
That shim exists to substitute one hook (see its header) and re-exports
`react-native-web`, which ships no type declarations at all — so it cannot
be the type source for anything. Checking the stories against real React
Native types is also the stricter and more honest contract: the native pane
is a claim about what a React Native consumer renders.
SCOPE: stories only. `workbench/react-native.ts`, `workbench/leaf-pair.tsx`
and `.storybook/` are excluded — the first cannot typecheck (untyped
`react-native-web`), and dragging the other two in would mean resolving
Storybook's own config types through this program for no gain. Widening
this include is a real change; read this block before doing it.
